readings: Match laboratory records to patients on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped) and group by patient ID and sex. For each patient, find their average white blood cell count (`WBC`) and their average hemoglobin-to-hematocrit ratio (`HGB`/`HCT`), ignoring missing values. Keep only patients whose ratio is greater than the mean of that ratio across all patients (missing values ignored). Show the patient ID, sex, average WBC, the ratio, and the ratio minus that mean. Sort by that gap, largest first with missing values last, return only the first 10 rows, and don't round anything.
queries:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.ID,
        p.SEX,
        AVG(l.WBC) AS avg_wbc,
        AVG(l.HGB / NULLIF(l.HCT, 0)) AS ratio
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(ratio) AS mean_ratio
    FROM patient_averages
)
SELECT
    pa.ID,
    pa.SEX,
    pa.avg_wbc,
    pa.ratio,
    pa.ratio - om.mean_ratio AS gap
FROM patient_averages AS pa
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS om
WHERE pa.ratio > om.mean_ratio
ORDER BY gap DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10
